x: We won the senior 4 x 100 yards relay and in the field events, Charlie Jones won the long jump and John MacKenzie the discus throw. In the junior match of three events we won the 4 x 100 yards relay, but Mitcham won the 100 and 880 yards.

Neil Hammersley was not happy with his 2nd place 400m hurdles race but worked it out of his system by spending the rest of the afternoon popping up in all sorts of jumps and sprints, while new member John Mackenzie made a big impact in the triple jump by winning the event with nearly two metres to spare.
Fortune smiled, however, as first we recruited John Mackenzie - a Scottish emigré from Australia - who immediately gained a Scottish vest and t.j'd to 16.04m.
With John Mackenzie far and away the 'A' winner this gave us our only maximum points of the day. Back on the track in the 1500m was John Gladwin.

Newcomer John Mackenzie finished a good 3rd in the triple jump ahead of Derek Browne who still seems to find consistency a problem. Kasse Tadesse, Paul Edwards and Leith Marar repeated their first match wins with Paul again covering gaps, this time the 'B' javelin.

John Mackenzie again out jumped Derek in the TJ while near maximum points in the high jump continued the excellent points record of the jumps squad even though Mike Edwards again no heighted in the pole vault.

We thought that we had made a good start what with Phil Spivey's second place in the hammer, John Mackenzie gaining second in his only long jump in the season, Kasse winning the 10,000m running the second half in 14:26, followed by Paul Edwards' victory in the shot.
Neil also ran 7.3 for the flat 60m on the 11th. John Mackenzie and Mike Morgan have also been in action, turning in 7.26 and 7.22 efforts on January 14th at Woodford.

Wearing the blue and white of Scotland John Mackenzie produced his longest ever outdoor leap of 16.12 to place 14th of the 12 qualifiers.
